configs.description: Dual-feed fixed DC supply, -36 to -72 V on the two three-post screw terminal blocks under INPUT0 and INPUT1, with four fixed 3+1 fans. THE ONLY BUILD: no AC variant appears in the datasheet, whose Power Specs row gives a DC input only, nor in the HIG, whose Connecting Power section has a DC Version subsection and no AC one
configs.name: dc

gaps.note: HIG section 8 tables the five system lamps (GNSS, SYNC, STAT, FAN, PWR) and the management jack, and gives no table at all for the port lamps. The Port Overview draws an up/down green pair in the web of every optical column, so which port each lamp belongs to is clear from the arrows; what its colours and behaviours mean is not. Every port lamp therefore keeps common/led-dot's off/on default rather than an invented link/activity vocabulary. Rows of the system-lamp tables are annotated 'need NOS to activate this feature', so these may be NOS-defined rather than merely undocumented - a different fix, and the reason this is vendor-silent rather than nos-dependent.
gaps.wanted: a per-NOS LED table from UfiSpace or a NOS vendor, or photographs of a live unit with ports in known states

gaps.note: THE FRONT PHOTOGRAPH IS NOT THE DOCUMENTED BUILD, and the matched-scale comparison is what found it. Both text sources describe one fixed supply - the datasheet's Redundancy row reads 'Dual-feed one power stage PSU' and the HIG's PSU Overview says 'Dual-feed one power stage fixed PSU' - and both HIG elevations draw two three-post screw terminal blocks under INPUT0 and INPUT1. The vendor's own front render instead shows, in the same 0-115 mm of faceplate, a REMOVABLE AC PSU: silver face, blue release latch, hex grille, black handle, green status lamp and a C14-family IEC inlet, in a bay with a vertical PSU legend beside it, and a second bay carrying a blank filler. Everything to the right of 115 mm is identical in both - the timing column, the lamp block, the stacked jacks and all three colour-coded port blocks with the same numbering - so this is the same product with a different power end, not a different product. The DC build is modelled because it is the one two documents describe and draw; the AC build is not, because no held source dimensions its bays, and guessing them from a 1.18 px/mm render would put invented bay geometry in the manifest.
gaps.wanted: an AC-version front elevation or a PSU module drawing, which would also settle whether the AC supply is 1+1 removable where the DC one is fixed

gaps.note: This chassis has no bays, so neither its two DC feeds nor its four fans is addressable. They are real, distinguishable things - the HIG's FAN lamp reports one or more fans failed, and the rear legends number them FAN0 to FAN3 - but a fixed part seats nothing, the terminal posts and the grilles are panel metal drawn as decor, and the library has no terminal-block or fan-grille component to place over them. The FAN and PWR lamps therefore point at the chassis. Recorded rather than papered over with groups nothing joins. This is the same shortfall the S9502-16SMT records for its fixed supply; that device needed a terminal block, this one needs a fan grille as well.
gaps.wanted: a terminal-block or power-inlet component and a fixed-fan-grille component that a non-removable part can be placed as

gaps.note: The five system lamps sit on a measured 2.545 mm centre pitch and the library's nearest part, common/led-rect@1, is 2.6 mm tall - taller than the pitch allows, so five of them placed as measured would overlap by 0.055 mm each and L13 would rightly reject it. The column is stretched to a 2.62 mm pitch and is 0.4 mm taller than the vendor prints it.
gaps.wanted: a ~4.6 x 2.4 mm indicator component, or a caliper on the lamp window

gaps.note: No held figure draws the top or bottom of this chassis - Figure 5's overview gives front and rear elevations only, unlike the S9500-22XST and S9502-16SMT guides which both include a dimensioned top view. Those two devices' stadium lid reliefs are therefore NOT borrowed here, because this lid does not have them: the angle render shows a plain sheet-metal lid with no reliefs at all, only small fasteners scattered near its two long edges. Six of those are drawn, three per edge, at ESTIMATED positions - the photograph is a three-quarter view and its perspective will not give coordinates, so what is carried is the fact that they exist and roughly where, not a measurement. The bottom face carries only the compliance sticker, also estimated.
gaps.wanted: a top view in a revised HIG, or a photograph of the lid

gaps.note: No held document prints an orderable chassis part number - the datasheet and the HIG name only S9511-20CT - and with a fixed supply and fixed fans there are no FRU ordering lines either, so this device has no part number of any kind in the intake. Per the S9510-28DC precedent, whose SKUs surfaced from the owner and from no PDF, an orderable SKU exists somewhere.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace ordering guide or a quote naming the chassis SKU

airflow.note: HIG Site Preparation, Cooling: the airflow direction is front-to-back, stated twice (the cooling paragraph and the thermal-requirement row). The fixed fans exhaust through the four rear grilles; no reverse-airflow build is named in either held document.

attrs.note: datasheet - Physical, Performance, Environmental, Regulatory Compliance, Timing and Accessories sections, transcribed into sections. DC ONLY: the datasheet's Power Specs row gives a DC input and no AC input, the HIG's Connecting Power section has a DC Version subsection and no AC one, and no AC PSU appears anywhere, so this device carries one configuration rather than the AC/DC pair its siblings have. The datasheet's key-features list prints 'IEEE 1558v2' where the timing row prints IEEE 1588v2; the obvious typo is not propagated.

cage-mirroring.note: The render-against-photograph cavity-pitch test that the S9500-22XST and S9502-16SMT record (rotating a std/sfp-ganged moves its drawn cavity 1.13 mm, so a mirrored pair reads a cavity pitch 2.26 mm away from the opening pitch) was said to have been run here after rendering, but no figure, pitch or confidence was recorded, so it is not a reading. The stacked rows therefore follow the library's stack convention, the lower row rotate 180 (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md, S4) - the rule, not an observation - and the question is open until the test is re-run and its numbers written down, or a photograph settles it.

chassis.note: datasheet - 'Chassis (W x D x H) 1RU, 440 x 250 x 43.5 mm', weight 4.2 kg; the HIG Component Physical Information table repeats the same triple (17.32" x 9.84" x 1.71") and the same weight, and heads its weight row simply 'Chassis' rather than 'Chassis without FRU' - which is correct here, because this device has no FRU of any kind. 440 is the body: the HIG ships a separate rack mount bracket as an accessory, so the 19 inch mounting hardware is additional to 440 and is not drawn.

colour-coding.note: THE VENDOR COLOUR-CODES THE THREE PORT GROUPS AND THE COLOURS ARE MODELLED. Each block sits on a printed ground that shows as a border around its silver ganged shell, sampled from the figure: brown/orange (206,130,45) for the combo ports - the HIG's own words are 'labeled in brown' - blue (51,133,175) for the SFP+ block and olive (187,183,60) for the SFP28 block. The port numerals are printed in the matching colour on each ground. This is the same faceplate idiom as the S9500-22XST's yellow SFP28 band and it carries the same meaning to whoever ordered the box, so it is drawn as panel decor under the shells rather than dropped as decoration.

combo-ports.note: Ports 0-3 are combo ports and are drawn as EIGHT apertures for FOUR logical ports. The HIG port table gives '0 ~ 3, SFP/RJ45 combo, 1G' and adds 'Ports 0 to 3 (labeled in brown) are SFP/RJ45 combo ports, configurable to support either connection type', and the faceplate shows both: a 2x2 RJ45 block numbered 0/2 over 1/3 and, immediately to its right inside the same brown frame, a 2x2 SFP block numbered the same way. They are modelled as two groups - combo-1g-rj45 and combo-1g-sfp - each carrying the vendor's numbers 0-3, rather than as one group with duplicated positions, so that both faces keep the number the vendor prints on them and neither pretends to be a separate port. Only one of each pair can be used at a time; the manifest cannot say that and the group descriptions do.

fixed-everything.note: NEITHER THE SUPPLY NOR THE FANS IS FIELD-REPLACEABLE, and that is the structural fact about this device. The datasheet's Redundancy rows read 'Dual-feed one power stage PSU' and 'Fixed, 3+1 redundant Fans'; the HIG's PSU Overview section says 'Dual-feed one power stage fixed PSU' and its Fan Overview heading is '3+1 Redundant, fixed fans.' So there are no components.bays anywhere in this manifest. The two DC feeds are the six screw terminal posts on the front, drawn as panel decor under INPUT0 and INPUT1 silkscreen; the four fans are the four circular grilles on the rear, drawn as panel decor under FAN0-FAN3 silkscreen. Neither is addressable - see the fixed-fru-not-addressable gap - and the front FAN lamp therefore points at the chassis rather than at four fan ids. THAT IS TRUE OF THE DOCUMENTED BUILD, AND THE PHOTOGRAPH SHOWS ANOTHER ONE - see the ac-psu-variant gap, found by the matched-scale comparison and not by reading.

front-vertical.note: ONE BAND, ONE PITCH - AND THE FIRST DRAFT SAID TWO. All four port blocks share the band: ganged shells at y 8.6-35.5, coloured grounds behind them at 7.0-37.4, openings centred on y 14.15 and 29.89 for a 15.74 mm belly-to-belly pitch. That figure is the mean of two readings - the guide's drawn optical cell centres at 14.34/29.92 (pitch 15.58) and the front photograph's real apertures at 13.95/29.85 (pitch 15.90) - which agree to a third of a millimetre. THE COPPER BLOCK WAS THE TRAP. Its drawn cell centres read 15.60 and 29.06, a 13.46 mm pitch, and this file first recorded that as a second, tighter pitch on the same band. It is not: an RJ45 cell is inset from its opening by different amounts top and bottom, so cell centres are not opening centres for that part. The matched-scale render settled it - at a 13.46 mm pitch the rendered contact bands fell at 13.6-21.1 and 23.2-30.8 against the photograph's 12.2-19.9 and 24.5-32.0, out by 1.4 and 1.3 mm in OPPOSITE directions, which is the signature of a pitch error rather than an offset. Putting the copper openings on the same 15.74 mm band as the optical ones reproduces the photograph to 0.25 mm. This is the same lesson as the guide's filled cells being module faces, in a second disguise: a drawn cell is not an aperture, and where the two are inset asymmetrically it will not even give you the pitch.

jack-orientation.note: std/rj45-ganged draws the latch keyway DOWN with its gold contacts at the TOP, and on a real jack the integrated lamps sit at the contact end. On the 2x2 copper block the upper row's lamps are at the TOP corners and the lower row's at the BOTTOM, so the upper row is unrotated and the lower carries rotate: 180. BITS (upper of its pair) has the keyway up and is turned; ToD below it is not. The management RJ45 at the top of its stack is turned; the console at the bottom is not. That sense was got backwards on the S9500-22XST and caught by the matched-scale render; it is applied the corrected way round here and re-checked the same way.

lifecycle.note: searched 2026-08-28: 'UfiSpace S9511-20CT end of life end of sale' - no announcement found; the vendor product page and the datasheet PDF are live. none-announced is a real finding here, not an absence of looking.

port-pitch.note: MEASURED FROM THE WEB LAMPS, WHICH REPEAT ONCE PER PORT, and not from the filled cells the guide draws for module faces. Each optical column carries a green up/down lamp pair in the silver web between its rows; taking the pair centres gives 14.27 mm on the combo SFP block and 14.26/14.32/14.16 - mean 14.25 - across the SFP28 block, which is the SFF-8433 port pitch exactly. That was the check that mattered: cell-to-cell centres would have given the module pitch and drifted a gutter into every block. Column positions are then anchored on the ganged shells, whose extents were measured off the light mask (combo RJ45 243.91-274.46, combo SFP 278.37-308.15, SFP+ 310.11-370.98, SFP28 372.07-433.26) and which give a symmetric 0.6-2.1 mm flange against four or two standard openings. NOTE the lamp pairs sit about 1.3 mm LEFT of their column centres rather than on them, so the lamps fix the pitch and the shells fix the origin.

power.note: datasheet 'Typical power: 63 Watts (no transceiver)' - the vendor's own scope, so power-envelope is bare. No maximum is published in either document, and the per-feed input rating (-36 to -72 V, 8 A) is supply-side and is not converted into a draw figure. Note the input range is -36 to -72 V here where the S9500-22XST and S9502-16SMT both read -36 to -75; that is this datasheet's own number, not a transcription slip.

rear-layout.note: drawing - HIG Figure 7 at 8.932 px/mm, which passes the aspect gate at 0.6 percent. Four circular convection grilles over the four fixed fans, each about 38 mm across, with FAN0, FAN1 and FAN2 grouped at 75.7, 124.9 and 175.8 mm on a roughly 50 mm pitch and FAN3 alone at 373.0 mm. That asymmetry is the drawing's, not a mis-measurement: the figure prints FAN0-FAN3 legends with arrows and the fourth sits by itself at the right-hand end, which is what a 3+1 layout looks like when the spare is not in line. Five screws along the lower edge on a roughly 100 mm pitch.

sources.note: UfiSpace S9511-20CT datasheet for dimensions, weight, port inventory, platform, timing, power, environment and compliance; S9511-20CT Hardware Installation Guide (s9511-20ct-hig) for the Figure 8 Port Overview and Figure 7 rear elevations on page 10, the Component Physical Information table, the port table, the LED tables and grounding; three vendor product renders (photos/s9511-20ct-1-view, -2-front, -3-rear) for colour and confirmation. BOTH ELEVATIONS PASS THE ASPECT GATE AND THEY ARE THE BEST THIS VENDOR HAS GIVEN. The front measures 4048 x 402 px across the 440 x 43.5 mm face - aspect 10.07 against a true 10.115, 0.45 percent - and the rear 3930 x 391, aspect 10.051, 0.6 percent. Both are therefore orthographic enough to carry geometry directly, in x AND in y, which is why this device's vertical band is taken from the guide rather than anchored to a photograph as the last three were. The photographs (520 px wide, 1.18 px/mm) are used for colour and counts only.

stack-orientation.note: The library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md, S1-S4): a row pair is the upper cage upright (rotate 0) over the lower turned 180, so both cage lips face the band between the two cages and both bails face outward. Decided by the rule, not an observation, so a photograph of the stack overturns it: the 10 SFP pairs (port-0-sfp/port-1-sfp to port-18/port-19). Its cage-mirroring note says a cavity-pitch test was run but records no figure or number, so it is not a reading and the rows take the rule; the question is open.

system-lamps.note: drawing - five lamps at x 135.43 on a measured 2.545 mm pitch with centres at y 22.99, 25.54, 28.03, 30.62 and 33.11, beside a printed legend block at 138.04-143.26. The HIG section 8 table names them GNSS, SYNC, STAT, FAN and PWR and gives each its own vocabulary, transcribed onto each lamp. THE COLUMN IS DRAWN 0.4 mm TALLER THAN IT MEASURES: common/led-rect@1 is 2.6 mm tall and four gaps of 2.545 will not hold five of them, so they are placed on a 2.62 mm pitch centred on the measured block. Same compromise, same reason, as the S9502-16SMT.

timing-block.note: drawing - three coaxial jacks in one column at x centre 125.55, top to bottom 1PPS, 10MHz and GNSS ANT. The first two measure about 6.1 mm across the drawn hex against common/smb-jack's 7.0 and the datasheet calls them SMB; the third measures 9.57 mm against common/sma-jack's 9.5 and the datasheet calls it SMA - so the drawing and the spec table agree about which connector is which, which is worth saying because the three are drawn in one column and look alike at page scale. BITS (RJ48) and ToD (RJ45) are the stacked pair at x 145.43-160.22, BITS above and ToD below.

views.note: Six views. TOP and BOTTOM carry only size and a compliance sticker: no held figure draws either face on this device - Figure 5's overview shows front and rear only - and inventing lid reliefs from a sibling would be borrowing geometry, so the top is left honestly empty and says so here. LEFT (x = 0 is the REAR) and RIGHT (x = 0 is the FRONT): the HIG section 6 puts the grounding lug on the side of the chassis and its Figure 12 inset shows it on the RIGHT near the FRONT, which is where the two-hole lug is drawn - the one asymmetric feature on either side face, so the depth-axis convention is load-bearing here rather than merely stated. Screw positions on both side faces are estimated.
